# PART 1 – Credibility and tools {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 1 – 90 minutes
:::

::: notes
Part one, then. We start further back than you might expect, with what science is for, why anyone thinks it is in trouble, and the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset and disagreed. Then the vocabulary that separates three kinds of repetition, what open research proposes as a remedy, and the evidence: three very large studies, published together, that measured how often social-science findings survive being repeated, one of which supplies the case of today. We finish on the tools, because sharing, checking and repeating are all things that software either makes easy or makes impossible, and on the setup check that gets your own machine ready.
:::
